title: chore: bring dev into main without a release
description:
Brings `dev` into `main` with no tag and no release, so there is no Zenodo record and nothing goes to CRAN. `main` has nothing that `dev` lacks.

## What it carries

- **#44:** the `cran` job reads every warning and every note, one message at a time, and fails on anything not on its known list. A dead link, a bad DOI, or a new message next to a known one now turns it red.
- **#45:** the version becomes `0.1.1.9000`, the usual R label for "0.1.1 plus work not released yet", and the READMEs now say r-universe builds from `main`.

## What changes once this is on `main`

- The docs site and r-universe build from `main`, so both will show `0.1.1.9000`. Today they show `allele` and `n_matches` under the label 0.1.1, which CRAN's 0.1.1 does not have.
- The Monday `cran` run reads its workflow from `main`, so it starts using the new filter.
- `CITATION.cff` stays at 0.1.1, the newest release.

## Checked

Both PRs were reviewed and green before merging into `dev`, and `cran.yml` was triggered by hand on each branch, since a PR into `dev` does not run it. On the #45 run, CRAN's extra checks gave one note, "Version contains large components (0.1.1.9000)", which is on the known list, plus the usual slow-examples note. This PR runs the full set again, including `cran`, against `main`.

The next release will be 0.2.0.

title: chore: mark main as the development version 0.1.1.9000
description:
`main` says 0.1.1, the same as CRAN, but it is not the same code: it has the MyGene fix (#39) and the ClinVar `allele` argument and `n_matches` column (#40), which CRAN's 0.1.1 does not. The docs site and r-universe both build from `main`. So a reader can see `allele` documented, install 0.1.1 from CRAN, and get "unused argument", while both copies call themselves 0.1.1.

## The changes

**Version `0.1.1.9000`.** The usual R convention for "0.1.1 plus work not released yet". It never goes to CRAN; the next release will be 0.2.0, minor, since there is a new argument and a new column. NEWS already says "(development version)". `CITATION.cff` stays at 0.1.1, because its own comment says it describes the newest release.

**One new known message in the `cran` filter.** A `.9000` version makes R say "Version contains large components". I checked this with a throwaway package before relying on it. The "Insufficient package version" entry stays, for the short window after a release before the version moves to `.9000`.

**README.** Both READMEs said r-universe serves binaries of the latest release. It builds from the latest commit on `main` (it currently serves `0513992`, the #43 merge, labelled 0.1.1), so it has fixes before they reach CRAN. The line now says that.

## Tested

Built `bioclients_0.1.1.9000.tar.gz` and ran `R CMD check --as-cran --run-donttest` with CRAN's extra checks on, the way the `cran` job does, then ran `cran-messages.R` on the log:

- "Version contains large components (0.1.1.9000)" is accepted.
- "Insufficient package version" no longer appears.
- The slow-examples note is accepted, and nothing else came up in CRAN's extra checks.
- The only two unknowns were local to this machine: no pandoc, and the `''NULL''` directory. The runner has pandoc and no such directory.

`cran.yml` only runs on PRs into `main`, so it was also triggered by hand on this branch.

No code change. The next step is a `dev` to `main` merge with no tag and no release, which puts the new version label on the docs site and r-universe and the new filter on the Monday run.

title: ci: fail the CRAN check on any unknown warning or note
description:
The `cran` job is the CRAN dress rehearsal: `R CMD check` with CRAN's extra checks turned on, on PRs into `main` and every Monday. Its warning filter had three gaps.

## The gaps

**A known message hid the rest.** R puts several findings into one warning, and the filter passed the whole warning if any known phrase was in it. On #42 a "possibly invalid ROR IDs" message got through this way, sitting in the same warning as the known version message. That one was a network blip; the next might not be.

**Notes were never read.** A dead link or DOI comes out as a note, not a warning. I checked with a throwaway package whose URL answers 404: R reports it as a NOTE. So the weekly run could not catch the moved URL its own header said it existed for.

**The known list was out of date.** Three of its four phrases no longer apply: the `Remotes:` line is gone, biohttp is on CRAN, and bioclients is no longer a new submission.

## The fix

The check now ends with `.github/scripts/cran-messages.R`, which reads the check log, splits every warning and note into its separate messages, and fails on any message not on the known list. The list holds two entries, each with its reason: the version message between releases, and the slow-examples note, which is network time and is explained in `cran-comments.md`.

While testing, I found that `rcmdcheck::parse_check()` silently skips a note that has no detail under it. So the script also compares what it read with the log's own `Status:` line, and fails if the log reports more than it could read.

The workflow's header now says what the job can and cannot catch. A service that moved still passes, because examples return an envelope and print `NULL` instead of erroring. `test-live.R` is what checks the services, and no workflow runs it.

The filter lives in a script instead of inline in the workflow, so the same code can be run locally against a saved check log.

## Tested

The script was run on five logs, built from real check output:

| Log | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Clean `cran` run from #43 | passes |
| No warnings or notes | passes |
| The #42 run where the ROR message slipped through | fails, naming the ROR message |
| A throwaway package with a dead link | fails, naming the 404 URL |
| A note with no detail | fails, saying the counts do not match |

`cran.yml` only runs on PRs into `main`, so this PR into `dev` does not run it. It was triggered by hand on this branch with `workflow_dispatch` to see it pass on GitHub.

## One thing to expect

A passing network failure, like the ROR one, now turns the job red. A re-run clears it. Red for an unknown message is the point: it means look.

title: feat(vep): sort, dedupe, and throttle before chunking in vep_variants_all
description:
A live case's coding lane can send every variant to vep_variants_all() in VCF read order, including duplicates a multiallelic split produces, and an unpaced burst of one-request-per-chunk can trip Ensembl's rate limiter partway through a run.

## What changed

- Input is put in genome order and a repeated variant (same chrom/pos/ref/alt) is sent once, not once per occurrence, before chunking. The external contract does not change: still one row per input, in input order. A duplicate's positions now always carry the same answer, which was not guaranteed before when duplicates could land in different chunks and see different transient failures.
- New vep_default_throttle() (1 request/second), applied by default via a new throttle parameter forwarded to biohttp::post_json_many(); pass throttle = NULL to disable.
- A stable dispatch order also gives biohttp's per-chunk cache (keyed on the exact request body) a real chance to hit between two calls that share a variant background.

## Local checks

Full suite: 1099 pass (1088 existing + 11 new), 1 skip (live-gated). lintr: 0 lints. prek: clean.

title: feat: VEP options and batching, gnomAD frequencies by id, ClinVar throttle, MyGene chunking
description:
## Summary

Six small commits from an audit of the VEP, gnomAD, ClinVar and MyGene clients.

### VEP

- **Bug fix.** `vep_parse_batch()` rebuilt its match key from `seq_region_name`, `start` and `allele_string`. VEP left-trims and renumbers indels (an insertion sent as `1 55516888 . T TA . . .` comes back as start 55516889, `-/A`), so every indel returned the empty row. Results are now matched on the echoed `input` line first, then `vcf_string` (requested with `vcf_string=1`), with the rebuilt key kept as a fallback for SNVs. A delins is re-anchored in `vcf_string` too, which is why `input` comes first.
- `vep_variants()` takes an `options` list, defaulting to `vep_default_options()`. The supported flags are documented there; `dbNSFP` is refused for the reason in the file header.
- `vep_parse_element()` adds `transcript`, `gene_id`, `biotype`, `hgvsc`, `hgvsp`, `canonical`, `codons`, `amino_acids`, `cadd_phred`, `cadd_raw`, `revel`, the four `spliceai_ds_*` scores, `spliceai_max` and `lof`, all `NA` when the flag was not asked.
- New `vep_parse_colocated()` reads the dbSNP record beside a variant: `rsid`, gnomAD genome and exome frequencies with their per-population maximum, and the clinical significance of the allele that was asked (from `clin_sig_allele`, so a multi-allelic site does not hand one allele another's call). `vep_parse_batch()` carries these columns.
- New `vep_variants_all()` chunks any number of variants at the 200 limit and dispatches through `biohttp::post_json_many()`. One row per input in input order; a failed chunk becomes `NA` rows with the envelope status in a `status` column, following `gnomad_constraints()`.

### gnomAD

- `gnomad_variant_id()`, `gnomad_frequency_by_id()` (lookup by `chrom-pos-ref-alt`, which names one allele where an rsID names a site) and `gnomad_frequencies()`, alias-batched and chunked like `gnomad_constraints()`.
- `gnomad_parse_variant()` and `gnomad_parse_variants()` return `variant_id`, `rsid`, exome and genome `af`/`ac`/`an`/`nhomalt`, `grpmax_af`/`grpmax_an`/`grpmax_id`, `faf95`, `faf95_pop`, `filters`. The API does not serve grpmax, so it is derived from the per-group counts with the bottlenecked groups excluded, and that is documented.
- An absent variant comes back from gnomAD as a 200 with `variant: null` and a `Variant not found` entry in `errors`, in both the single and the aliased form. That is treated as an answer rather than a query failure.
- The alias cost cap was re-verified live for the variant query: 25 aliases with the full selection set answer, 26 return `Query is too expensive (26). Maximum allowed cost is 25.` So cost is one per alias regardless of fields; the chunk size stays at 20.

### ClinVar

- `clinvar_classification()` throttles by default at the documented E-utilities rate (3 a second, 10 with `NCBI_API_KEY`), following `CLINGEN_THROTTLE`, and sends `tool` and `email` from `BIOHTTP_CALLER_IDENTITY` and `BIOHTTP_CONTACT_EMAIL` when set. Blank means omitted.

### MyGene

- `mygene_genes()` chunks at 1000 identifiers, dispatches through `post_json_many()` and merges in input order.

## Fixtures

Recorded live on 2026-08-30 from public sites, no patient data:

- `vep_region_indels.json`: TP53 p.Pro72Arg (SNV), a PCSK9 intronic insertion, CFTR p.Phe508del (deletion), a TP53 exonic delins, with the default flags plus `vcf_string=1`.
- `vep_region_indels_freq.json`: the same four sites with `af_gnomadg=1&af_gnomade=1&CADD=1&SpliceAI=1&REVEL=1&hgvs=1`.
- `gnomad_variant_present.json` and `gnomad_variant_absent.json`.

Transcript arrays are trimmed to the MANE Select plus one other transcript, PubMed lists to three entries, and the HGDP/1000 Genomes population subsets dropped, so the files stay small while the JSON shape stays faithful.

## Checks

`devtools::document()`, `devtools::test()` (1088 passing, offline) and `prek run --all-files` before each commit. `DESCRIPTION` version untouched; `NEWS.md` has a development-version section.

title: fix: index every exported function in the pkgdown reference
description:
The pkgdown build fails once its dependencies resolve, because the reference index listed 32 of 125 exported functions and pkgdown treats an unlisted export as an error rather than a warning.

The index had never been extended past Batch A, so everything from Batch B onward was missing: 94 topics across 22 services.

## What changed

One section per service, as before, but ordered by the question being asked rather than alphabetically. A caller arrives knowing they want a population frequency or a pathway, not knowing that gnomAD or Reactome is the thing that answers it.

Each section's `desc` states the one thing about that service a caller has to know before using it, rather than restating the title:

- MyVariant always sends `assembly = "hg38"`, without which GRCh38 coordinates come back `notfound`
- Ensembl REST numbers exons in transcription order, so on the minus strand exon 1 has the highest coordinate
- IMPC never reports 0, because "never phenotyped" and "phenotyped with no result" are indistinguishable
- Europe PMC does report 0, because a gene with no literature is not an outage
- PanelApp returns the traffic-light level as published rather than as a weight

## Verification

Every export is indexed exactly once, checked against `NAMESPACE`:

```
exports: 125 | indexed: 126 | duplicates: 0
exported but not indexed: (none)
indexed but not exported: bioclients-package
```

The 126th is the package doc topic, which is not an export. `pkgdown::build_reference_index()` completes locally.

## Note

This does not make CI green on its own. Every bioclients job currently fails earlier, at dependency resolution, because `biohttp (>= 0.3.0)` is not installable from a private repo. That is a separate decision.

title: feat: follow the biohttp 0.1.0 release and add the hex logo
description:
Six commits that accumulated locally while the repo stayed off CI. Supersedes #1,
whose commits are the first two here.

## What is in it

| Commit | |
| --- | --- |
| `fix: index every exported function in the pkgdown reference` | all 125 exports, one section per service |
| `fix: build the pkgdown site where the workflow uploads it from` | `build_site_github_pages()` defaults `dest_dir` to `docs`, overriding `destination: _site`, so the upload found nothing |
| `feat: add the hex logo` | plus the favicon set pkgdown builds from it |
| `ci: run the workflows only at the release gate` | and gitleaks joins the local hooks |
| `fix: follow the biohttp 0.1.0 release` | the pin, `Remotes:`, and dropping `webfakes` |
| `docs: add a changelog and describe where the checks run` | `NEWS.md`, which the navbar was silently dropping |

## The blocking one

biohttp renumbered to 0.1.0 for its public release, so the `>= 0.3.0` pin here no
longer resolved at all: installing biohttp from main and loading this package
failed outright. biohttp is public but not on CRAN, so `Remotes:` is what lets a
clean runner find it. Verified by installing from GitHub with `GITHUB_PAT` and
`GITHUB_TOKEN` both blanked, which is the access a CI job gets by default.

`Remotes:` has to come back out before any CRAN submission. That is recorded in
its commit message.

## Why this is one PR rather than six

The commits are separate and each one installs on its own, but stacking them as
PRs would mean a chain whose bases are each other. `dev` is the integration
branch; this is what it is for.

## Verified locally

- `prek run --all-files` passes, gitleaks included
- full suite green against biohttp 0.1.1
- `rcmdcheck` with `--as-cran`: 0 errors, 1 warning, 1 note

The warning is entirely private-repo and pre-CRAN: three 404 URLs, `biohttp` not
on a repository, and `Remotes` flagged as an unknown field. The note is an
`R CMD check` artefact on Windows that a trivial control package reproduces.

## No Actions minutes

The workflows in this branch only fire on a pull request into `main`, so this PR
runs nothing, and merging it into `dev` runs nothing either.

title: docs: correct the README and give the package its own
description: Both READMEs had drifted past out-of-date into misleading. ## Root README - **The service table listed 8 of 29.** It now lists all 29, grouped by the question being asked rather than alphabetically, matching how `_pkgdown.yml` already orders the reference index. All 106 function names in it were checked against `NAMESPACE`; none is invented. - **Installation said neither package was published**, and warned CI could not resolve biohttp. biohttp is public, tagged `v0.1.1`, on r-universe, and the `Remotes:` line resolves it on a clean runner. - **The roadmap had phase 3 as "not started"** when it was finished, and did not mention the confirmation that genuinely has not happened. Now phase 3 is confirming the ported behaviour against live services, phase 4 is the variant-reviewer migration, which has a working demonstration. - `Imports` omitted `httr2`. - Fixtures were credited entirely to `variant-reviewer`; most came from `genescout`. ## New `pkg-r/README.md` Modelled on `biobouncer/pkg-r/README.md`: opens with the logo, points at the root README for what the project is, then goes to usage. This is what puts the hex on the documentation site. pkgdown 2.2.1 has no logo slot in its navbar template, so a logo only reaches a site through a README inside the package, and this package had none. The home page was previously the DESCRIPTION paragraph and nothing else. Verified after rebuilding: the home page now carries ``, which it did not before, and the news page still builds. Every usage example was run against the installed package before being written down, including the `no_data` case and the batch that returns a row of `NA` in input order. ## Checks `prek run --all-files` passes, and `rcmdcheck --as-cran` is unchanged at 0 errors, 1 warning, 1 note, both of which are the known private-repo and environmental ones. No Actions minutes: the workflows only fire on a pull request into `main`.

title: feat: add an allele argument to clinvar_classification()
description:
Fixes #40. `clinvar_classification()` kept the first record ClinVar's search returned, and for many terms that is not the variant asked for.

## Wider than the issue

The issue is about rsIDs. Checking it showed the same thing for HGVS names, and for other well-known variants:

| Term | First record ClinVar lists | Wanted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rs113488022` | VCV000040389, BRAF V600G | V600E |
| `NM_004333.6:c.1799T>A` | VCV000178963, BRAF **I208V**, a different variant at a different position | V600E |
| `rs121913343` | VCV000634682, TP53 R273G | R273C |

Only an SPDI such as `NC_000007.14:140753335:A:T`, or a VCV accession, matched a single record. The help page also said "An rsID is the term that works best", which steered callers to the weak form.

## The change

- The client fetches every record esearch returns in the one esummary call, so it is still two requests.
- New argument `allele`: a protein change such as `"V600E"` or `"p.Val600Glu"`. It is matched against each record's own `protein_change` field, split into its list (`"V600E, V512E, ..."`), not searched for in the title. Three-letter codes, `p.(...)`, lower case, stops and frameshifts are brought into ClinVar's form first.
- With `allele` and no record that has it: `no_data`, with a detail naming the term and the allele. Falling back to the first record would bring the bug back.
- New column `n_matches`: how many records fit the request. Above 1 means the row may be for a different variant.
- Without `allele` the first record is still returned, so existing code keeps working. `allele` comes after `throttle`, so no positional call changes meaning.
- esummary answers a UID it cannot summarise with a record that holds only `error`. Those records are skipped, so a dead UID listed first no longer gives a row of `NA` marked `ok`. Only error records gives `no_data`. Found in review; both tests for it fail without the change.
- `retmax=20` is now sent explicitly, so the record limit is visible in the code. It was already ClinVar's default.
- The help page names the terms that match one record, SPDI and VCV, and no longer recommends an rsID. The example shows both ways.

## Checked live

- `rs113488022` with `allele = "V600E"` or `"p.Val600Glu"` gives VCV000013961. With `"V600K"` it gives `no_data`.
- The HGVS name with `allele = "V600E"` gives VCV000013961, not I208V.
- `rs121913343` with `allele = "R273C"` gives VCV000043594.
- SPDI and VCV give one record, `n_matches = 1`.
- Without `allele`, `rs113488022` still gives V600G, now with `n_matches = 2`.

## Tests

- Two fixtures recorded live for `rs113488022` with the client's own requests, the esearch and the esummary for both records.
- Default behaviour with `n_matches`, `allele` in one-letter and three-letter form, an allele no record has, an `NA` allele, more than one allele refused before any request, `retmax` sent, and the protein change helpers.
- Every request count is pinned: still two.
- `clinvar_40389.json` and the existing tests are unchanged.
- `test-live.R` checks that the HGVS name still matches more than one record, and that `allele` picks V600E.

Locally, merged with `main` so both #39 and #40 are in: 1,143 tests pass, 0 lints with CI's rules, hooks clean, no commented lines in examples.

This is the ClinVar half of samuelbharti/variant-reviewer#27, so it unblocks part of #35.

title: fix: keep the reference Ensembl id when MyGene lists several
description:
Fixes #39. `mygene_gene()` and `mygene_genes()` returned `NA` for `ensembl_gene` whenever MyGene maps a gene to more than one Ensembl id, PTEN and MUC16 among them.

## Cause

MyGene sends `ensembl` as one object for most genes and as a list of objects when a gene has more than one id. `mygene.R` read it with `biohttp::pluck_at(hit, "ensembl", "gene")`, which does `x[["gene"]]`, and on a list without names that gives `NULL`. Both paths build their row in `mygene_row()`, so both broke.

## Taking the first id is not the fix

The list is not ordered reference first. Checked live:

| Gene | First id in the list | Where it sits | Reference id, and its place |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PTEN | ENSG00000171862 | chr 10 | same, 1st |
| HLA-A | ENSG00000235657 | alternate haplotype | ENSG00000206503, 8th of 8 |
| C4A | ENSG00000244207 | alternate haplotype | ENSG00000244731, 4th of 4 |
| KIR2DL1 | ENSG00000278495 | alternate haplotype | ENSG00000125498, 29th of 34 |

Taking the first would give HLA-A an id that looks normal and that Open Targets and the Human Protein Atlas do not know.

## The fix

The client also asks for `genomic_pos.chr` and `genomic_pos.ensemblgene`, which pair each id with its chromosome. With several ids it keeps the one on a reference chromosome (1 to 22, X, Y, MT). For genes in the region X and Y share, such as SHOX, X wins. A gene whose ids all sit on alternate haplotypes, such as HLA-DRB3, gets `NA`. A gene with one id keeps it, as before.

## Checked live

- PTEN, MUC16 and NF1 give the ids the issue expects. TP53 is unchanged.
- HLA-A, C4A and KIR2DL1 give their reference id. SHOX and CD99 give the X id. HLA-DRB3 gives `NA`.
- With PTEN's id, `opentargets_gene_diseases()` returns 20 diseases and `hpa_gene()` finds PTEN, which the NEWS entry says.

## Tests

- Two fixtures recorded live with the client's own request: `mygene_pten.json` (patch id, reference first) and `mygene_hla_a.json` (reference id last).
- Inline bodies for SHOX, HLA-DRB3, a list with no `genomic_pos`, a single id, and the batch path.
- A URL check that `genomic_pos` is requested.
- `mygene_tp53.json` is unchanged, as a ported fixture should be.
- `test-live.R` checks that MyGene still sends PTEN's ids as a list. The section heading there said "The five behaviours", so it no longer has a number.

Locally: 1,111 tests pass, 0 lints with CI's rules, hooks clean.

Same read in genescout: samuelbharti/genescout#48.

title: chore: archive 0.1.1 on Zenodo and add a CRAN downloads badge
description:
Two small changes after the 0.1.1 release.

## Zenodo DOI for 0.1.1

0.1.1 is on CRAN since 2026-09-15 but had no git tag or GitHub release, so Zenodo had nothing to archive. I tagged `v0.1.1` at `4a37626`, the commit the CRAN tarball was built from, and created the release. Zenodo archived it as `10.5281/zenodo.23221627`.

To pick the commit, I compared CRAN's own tarball with git file by file. All 260 package files match `4a37626`. `DESCRIPTION` differs only in layout and in the fields CRAN adds, and its `Packaged` time is nine minutes after `4a37626` was merged. Today's `main` has README edits that CRAN never saw, so the tag does not go there.

`CITATION.cff` now lists the 0.1.1 DOI next to 0.1.0. `date-released` changes from 2026-09-07, the day the tarball was built, to 2026-09-15, the day CRAN published it.

The concept DOI, `10.5281/zenodo.21770870`, now resolves to 0.1.1. The badges and the README citation use the concept DOI, so they need no change.

## CRAN downloads badge

Both READMEs show the total CRAN downloads next to the CRAN status badge. The badge link goes to the CRAN page.

Closes #37
Closes #32, since both READMEs already carry the CRAN badge and `install.packages("bioclients")` is the first install line.

title: docs: use plain section names and cut what a learner does not need
description:
Two passes over the README, both aimed at someone learning the package rather than someone maintaining it.

## The headings were questions

"What is in it", "What it does not do", "The shape of a client", and seven more in the service catalogue reading "Which gene is this", "What is known about this variant" and so on. Scanning for a section meant reading every heading.

They are plain nouns now:

| Was | Now |
| --- | --- |
| A first call | Usage |
| Why | Motivation |
| What it does not do | Scope |
| What is in it | Services |
| Which gene is this | Genes |
| What is known about this variant | Variants |
| Is this gene linked to disease, and is it druggable | Disease and drugs |
| What does the protein look like | Proteins |
| Where is it expressed, and what does it do | Expression and function |
| What phenotype does it cause | Phenotypes |
| Who has written about it | Literature |
| Citing bioclients | Citation |

## Cut

**The shape of a client** described the client and parser halves and how the tests use them. That is how the package is built, not how it is used, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers it.

**The drift table** in Motivation listed how many copies of each client exist in other repositories. Hand-maintained, about other repos, on this front page. The point fits in a sentence.

## Reworded

The scope list was five bolded items each opening with "No". It now says the same thing as a short paragraph, without arguing with the reader.

334 lines at the start of this pass, 184 now.

title: docs: trim the READMEs to what each page is for
description:
Two files, one idea: each page says what it is, and says it once.

## The root README

334 lines down to 191. What went:

| Section | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Roadmap | A phase table, a work log and a status report on the front page. The live half is now #35 |
| Dependencies | `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers it |
| No compiled code | `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers it, and in a fuller form |
| Testing | `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers it. One sentence in it appeared twice, 26 lines apart |
| Repository layout | `CONTRIBUTING.md` covers it, and the section ended by saying so |
| Three design essays | Good writing, wrong place. They sat inside a catalogue of clients |
| The batch example | `pkg-r/README.md` carries it, and that is the page that needs it |

The seven question headings and their tables stay. They are what a caller
arrives for, and they answer the question a caller actually has.

Two claims were wrong:

- The text said 29 clients while the tables under it listed 30 rows, because
  gnomAD answers two different questions and takes two rows. The count is gone
  and the tables speak for themselves.
- The citation section named 0.1.0 as the version to pin, and said every release
  is archived. Zenodo holds 0.1.0 only, and CRAN is at 0.1.1.

## The CRAN page

Most readers reach `pkg-r/README.md` from CRAN, with none of the repository
around it. It now carries a licence line, a licence badge and a link to the
documentation site. It no longer points at `README.md` and `PLAN.md`, neither of
which ships in the tarball.

The hand-written excerpt of `NEWS.md` is replaced by a link to the changelog.
One copy to keep current instead of two, and the old copy already conceded it
was incomplete.

## Not done here

A CRAN downloads badge was tried and dropped. bioclients reached CRAN on
2026-09-15, so cranlogs answers `null` for the grand total and `0/month` for the
last month. That reads as failure rather than as a package nobody has had time
to download. It is worth adding once the numbers are real.

title: docs: say that bioclients is on CRAN
description:
bioclients reached CRAN on 2026-09-15 at 0.1.1. Both READMEs still said otherwise:

> bioclients is not on CRAN yet.

## Changes

The install section leads with CRAN, and keeps the other two routes:

```r
install.packages("bioclients")
```

`pak::pak()` stays for the development version, and r-universe for prebuilt binaries.

`pkg-r/README.md` had no badges at all. That file is what CRAN renders on the package page, so it needs to stand on its own. It now carries the same block as the root README:

```
lifecycle · CRAN status · R-CMD-check · r-universe · DOI
```

## On the downloads badge

It is deliberately absent. cranlogs has no rows for a package published yesterday, and the badge renders this today:

```
aria-label="CRAN downloads null"
```

Worth adding once the counts appear, which takes a day or two after publication.

## Checked

Every badge was fetched and read rather than assumed:

```
CRAN status     CRAN 0.1.1
r-universe      r-universe: 0.1.1
lifecycle       lifecycle: stable
R-CMD-check     r.yml exists in .github/workflows
DOI             resolves, 302
```

`stable` is the lifecycle stage because the package is on CRAN, where a release has users who can be broken by a change.

title: ci: accept the warning that follows publication
description:
The `cran` job fails on every pull request:

```
0 errors | 1 warning | 0 notes

Unexpected warnings:
 checking CRAN incoming feasibility ... WARNING
Insufficient package version (submitted: 0.1.1, existing: 0.1.1)
Days since last update: 1
```

Nothing is wrong with the package. `R CMD check --as-cran` compares the version in the repository against the version on CRAN, and warns when they match. They match because 0.1.1 was published on 2026-09-15 and nothing has changed since, which is the normal state between releases.

The job already keeps a list of warnings that are not defects:

```r
known <- c("Remotes", "not in the CRAN or BioC", "New submission")
```

All three describe the state *before* publication. None covers the state after it, so the check started failing on the day the package went live. Main's last passing run was 2026-09-14, the day before.

This adds the fourth case.

## Not a version bump

Bumping to 0.1.2 would also clear the warning, and would be wrong. The last commit on main is 2026-09-07 and CRAN published on 2026-09-15, so there is nothing a 0.1.2 would contain. `NEWS.md` has no 0.1.2 section for the same reason. `Days since last update: 1` is CRAN noting the same thing from its side.

## Also

The failure message said "the known biohttp one", which stopped being accurate once the list held more than one entry.

title: docs: say what the package is for in the Description field
description:
One commit. The `Description` field now opens with what the package is for rather than how it is built. Same facts, same length, the design points still there but after the thing a reader wants first.

The five references are untouched: same order, same `authors (year) <doi:...>` form, no space after `doi:`. `CITATION.cff` carried the same old wording in its abstract and now matches.

Merging republishes the docs site and puts the new text on the package page. This is the last change before submission.

title: docs: say what the package is for in the Description field
description:
The `Description` field opened with three sentences about how the package is built: request half, parser half, canonical structure, pure, stored response. None of that means anything to someone reading the CRAN page who has not used it.

This is the same problem the README headline and the repo description had. Those were fixed; this field was missed, and it matters more. It is what shows on the CRAN package page, in `packageDescription()`, on r-universe and in search results.

## Before

> One client per biological database, each split into a request half that calls the service and a parser half that turns a response body into a canonical structure. The parser is pure, so it is tested against a stored response with no network.

## After

> Look up genes, variants and proteins from R, without writing a client for every biological web service. Each service gets one client that makes the request and returns a table. Parsing is a separate function that needs no network, so it can run on a saved response and be tested offline.

Same facts, same length. The design points are all still there, just after the thing a reader wants first.

## References untouched

All five kept, same order, same `authors (year) <doi:...>` form, no space after `doi:`. Verified after the edit: 5 DOIs present, 0 occurrences of `doi: ` with a space.

Worth keeping them even though this package implements no method of its own, because biobouncer got asked for references on its first submission and is now on CRAN at 0.1.4 with them in place. Cheap insurance against a resubmission cycle.

`Twenty-nine services are covered` became `The services covered include`, so there is one less number to go stale.

## CITATION.cff

Its `abstract` carried the old wording. Both say the same thing now.

title: docs: reference every topic and simplify the headlines
description:
Two commits, both documentation. No code or behaviour change.

**Every exported topic now has a `References` section.** Nine did not: the gnomAD frequency functions and the VEP option functions from #15 and #16, which landed after the CRAN prep added references to everything else. `cran-comments.md` tells the reviewer that every topic has one, so this was a claim that would not survive a spot check. Each now inherits from the main entry point in its file, the way the rest of the file already does.

Counts fixed at the same time: `cran-comments.md` and the 0.1.1 NEWS section said 125 exported topics, it is 134. The 0.1.0 section still says 125, which is correct for that release.

**Both READMEs open with a plain line now.** The old one was "One client per biological database, each with a pure parser that runs offline", which describes how the package is built rather than what it is for.

## Verified

Local `R CMD check --as-cran`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 3 notes. Two are this machine, missing pandoc and a `''NULL''` directory. `checking Rd cross-references ... OK` and `checking for missing documentation entries ... OK`, so the new `@inherit` lines resolve.

Also checked while reviewing for submission: all 5 `Description` DOIs confirmed through CrossRef against the author and year claimed, all 29 help page DOIs resolve, all 8 dependencies are on CRAN, all 4 `DESCRIPTION` URLs return 200, and the licence file names both copyright holders to match the two `cph` roles.

title: docs: make both headlines say what the package is for
description:
The old line was "One client per biological database, each with a pure parser that runs offline". That describes how the package is built, not what you would use it for, and none of those words mean anything until you already know it.

Both READMEs now open the same way:

> Look up genes, variants and proteins from R. One consistent way to call gnomAD, ClinVar, UniProt, Ensembl and the other databases you already use, instead of writing a client for each one.

The package README also stopped opening with "This directory holds the R package". That file is what pkgdown builds the docs home page from, where there is no directory to speak of. The design explanation is still there, just in plainer words and below the headline.

Matches the repo description, which changed the same way.

title: docs: give the new topics a References section
description:
Found while reviewing the package for submission.

## The problem

`cran-comments.md` tells the reviewer that **every** exported topic has a `References` section. Nine did not:

`gnomad_frequencies`, `gnomad_frequency_by_id`, `gnomad_parse_variant`, `gnomad_parse_variants`, `gnomad_variant_id`, `vep_default_options`, `vep_default_throttle`, `vep_parse_colocated`, `vep_variants_all`.

All of them landed in #15 and #16, after the CRAN prep added references to everything else. That is a claim a reviewer would check and find false, which is the worst kind to leave in a submission.

## The fix

Each one now inherits the reference from the main entry point in its file, using `@inherit gnomad_constraint references` or `@inherit vep_variants references`, which is how the rest of each file already does it.

All 134 exported topics have one now. `bioclients-package.Rd` still does not, which is right: it documents no function.

## Counts

`cran-comments.md` and the 0.1.1 section of `NEWS.md` said 125 exported topics. It is 134.

The two mentions of 125 in the **0.1.0** section of `NEWS.md` are left alone on purpose. 0.1.0 really did have 125, and rewriting that would misstate history.

## Also verified while reviewing

- all 5 `Description` DOIs confirmed through CrossRef, each matching the author and year claimed
- all 29 help page DOIs resolve, exactly as `cran-comments.md` says
- all 8 dependencies are on CRAN, biohttp at 0.1.2
- all 4 `DESCRIPTION` URLs return 200
- `DESCRIPTION`, `CITATION.cff` and the NEWS heading all say 0.1.1
- the licence file names both copyright holders, matching the two `cph` roles
- 56 `\donttest{}`, 0 `\dontrun{}`

title: chore: prepare 0.1.1 for the CRAN submission
description:
Four commits since the last release PR. All documentation, metadata and examples. No behaviour changes.

## What is in it

**Funding corrected.** Anthropic, PBC is no longer listed as a funder. Posit's line moves from present to past tense: it funded early work rather than funding it now. Posit stays as copyright holder and funder, and the licence files are unchanged.

**CRAN Cookbook pass.** Checked the package against the [Cookbook](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/) chapter by chapter. Most of it was already right: Title Case, quoted software names in `Description`, the doi format, a `\value` tag on all 134 help pages that need one, no `setwd`/`options`/`print`/`cat`, nothing written outside `tempdir()`, a 0.24 MB tarball.

One thing was wrong. Three examples still used `\dontrun{}`: `gnomad_frequencies`, `gnomad_frequency_by_id` and `vep_variants_all`. They arrived in #15 and #16, after the earlier pass moved the other 53 to `\donttest{}`. They are the same kind of public keyless request, so there was no reason to treat them differently. Now every example uses `\donttest{}`, 56 of them. Changed in the `.R` files and re-documented, because the Cookbook warns CRAN turns down a resubmission where only the `.Rd` changed.

**README.** pak is the first install option now, r-universe second. Two claims near the top were wrong: it said neither package is on CRAN when biohttp has been there since 0.1.2, and it explained a `Remotes:` line we had already removed. "No compiled code" dropped from 25 lines to 12. The export count said 125 and is 134. Phase 4 claimed the variant-reviewer migration was demonstrated when only the biohttp half ever was, so it is split into 4a and 4b.

**Citation.** `CITATION.cff` now says 0.1.1, dated 2026-09-07, so the tag lands on a tree whose metadata is already right.

## Checks

Local `R CMD check --as-cran` on the built tarball: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 3 notes. Two of those are this machine only, missing pandoc and a `''NULL''` directory. On CRAN it should be one: new submission.

With all 56 `\donttest{}` examples: `checking examples with --run-donttest ... [59s] OK` and `checking tests ... [51s] OK`. That is 110 seconds against CRAN's 10 minute limit. No example tripped the 5 second threshold in that run, which is the point `cran-comments.md` makes: which ones are slow depends on which service is slow that minute.

This PR also runs `cran.yml`, which is the only place the 56 example count gets timed on a clean runner.

## After this merges

Tag `v0.1.1`, cut the release, let Zenodo mint the version DOI, add that DOI to `CITATION.cff`, then submit.

title: chore: point the citation at 0.1.1
description:
`CITATION.cff` still said 0.1.0. The tag should land on a tree whose citation metadata already says 0.1.1, so this goes in before the release rather than after.

`date-released` moves to 2026-09-07.

The `identifiers` list still shows 0.1.0 and its DOI, which is right for now. Zenodo mints the 0.1.1 DOI when the release is cut, and it gets added then. The `doi` field does not change: that is the concept DOI and it always resolves to the newest release.

title: docs: put pak first and cut the stale bits from the README
description:
## pak first

`pak::pak("samuelbharti/bioclients/pkg-r")` is now the first install option, r-universe second.

## Two claims were wrong

The install section said **"Neither package is on CRAN"**. biohttp has been on CRAN since 0.1.2.

It also explained the `Remotes:` line and said it has to come out before a CRAN submission. We took it out during the CRAN prep, so that paragraph described a file that no longer looks like that.

Both were the first thing a visitor read.

## Less complexity

**"No compiled code" went from 25 lines to 12.** It carried a ranked list of where the time actually goes, with numbers for concurrent fan-out, batch endpoints and caching, and named C libraries to reach for if that ever changed. That is design-note material. The section keeps the point and the number behind it: 210 ms on the network against 0.2 ms parsing.

The status line lost a clause about CRAN not taking a package whose dependency it does not have. True, but that is about CRAN's rules, not this package.

## Two things that were plain wrong

**The export count said 125.** It is 134. The VEP and gnomAD work added nine.

**Phase 4 claimed more than happened.** The row said the variant-reviewer move was "demonstrated, not landed". Only the biohttp half was ever demonstrated. The bioclients half was never attempted. Now split:

| 4a. Move `variant-reviewer` onto `biohttp` | shown to work, not landed |
| 4b. Move `variant-reviewer` onto `bioclients` | not started |

with a line saying 4b is the bigger half, and that variant-reviewer still has its own client per service, which is the duplication bioclients exists to remove.

## Checks

All three GitHub links return 200. 345 lines down to 331. Does not overlap with #21, so the merge order does not matter.

title: chore: follow the CRAN Cookbook on examples and check notes
description:
Checked the package against the [CRAN Cookbook](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/), chapter by chapter.

## Already fine

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Title in Title Case | `tools::toTitleCase()` returns it unchanged |
| Software names quoted in `Description` | 'AlphaFold', 'Ensembl', 'Open Targets', 'UniProt', 'biohttp', 'gnomAD' |
| References as `Authors (year) <doi:...>`, no space | all five correct |
| `\value` on every help page | 134 of 135; the one without is the package page, which does not need it |
| No `setwd()`, `options()`, `par()` without a reset | none in `R/` |
| No `print()` or `cat()` | none |
| No `install.packages()` or `library()` | none |
| No `<<-`, no bare `T`/`F` | none |
| Nothing written outside `tempdir()` | none |
| Tarball size | 0.24 MB, well under the 5 MB note |
| Total check time | about 3 minutes, limit is 10 |

`MIT + file LICENSE` is right even though the Cookbook warns about it. MIT is a template licence that needs YEAR and COPYRIGHT HOLDER filled in, so the file has to be there. The warning is for licences like GPL-3 that do not need one.

## One thing was wrong

Three examples still used `\dontrun{}`: `gnomad_frequencies`, `gnomad_frequency_by_id` and `vep_variants_all`. They arrived in #15 and #16, after the earlier pass moved the other 53 to `\donttest{}`, so they were missed.

The Cookbook says `\dontrun{}` is only for an example that truly cannot run. These can: they are public requests with no key, the same as the other 53. A reviewer comparing 53 against 3 for identical work would have asked why.

Every example now uses `\donttest{}`, 56 of them. Changed in the `.R` files and re-documented, not by editing `.Rd` directly, because the Cookbook warns CRAN turns down a resubmission where only the `.Rd` changed.

## Stale claims fixed

- "53 examples" was written into `cran-comments.md`, `NEWS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `cran.yml`. All say 56 now.
- `cran-comments.md` explained the slow-example note with `ensembl_gene_model` and `vep_variants`. The last real run flagged `vep_variants` (20.5s), `uniprot_features` (15.0s) and `diseases_channel` (5.5s). It now uses those numbers.
- It said "0 or 1 note". It is really 1 or 2, because the new submission note is always there.

## Checks

`R CMD check --as-cran` on the built tarball: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 3 notes. Two of those are this machine only, no pandoc and a `''NULL''` directory. On CRAN it should be one: new submission.

title: chore: correct who funded this
description:
Drops Anthropic, PBC as a funder, and changes Posit's line from present to past tense: it funded early work on this package rather than funding it now. Posit stays as copyright holder and funder in `Authors@R`, and the licence files are unchanged.

## Review notes

**Nothing is left inconsistent.** No Anthropic mention survives anywhere on the branch. `_pkgdown.yml` builds its home page sidebar from `roles: [aut, cre, ths, fnd]` rather than a hardcoded list, so the docs site follows `DESCRIPTION` on its own. `CITATION.cff` only lists the author, so there was nothing to change there.

**This branch is 23 commits behind `dev`,** cut before the 0.1.1 work, and three files changed on both sides: `README.md`, `pkg-r/DESCRIPTION` and `man/bioclients-package.Rd`. Given a stale branch reverted the Code of Conduct fix earlier this week, I trial-merged this one before opening it rather than assuming.

The merge is clean. Anthropic goes, and everything from the CRAN preparation survives: version 0.1.1, `biohttp (>= 0.1.2)`, no `Remotes:` line, and all five DOI references in `Description`.

title: feat: release 0.1.1 and prepare the CRAN submission
description:
Everything on `dev` since 0.1.0. 23 commits, 192 files.

This is also the first time `cran.yml` runs. It only fires on a pull request into `main`, so this run is the dress rehearsal for the submission itself.

## What is in it

**New work on four clients.** VEP gained an `options` list, `vep_variants_all()` for any number of variants, colocated dbSNP parsing, and sorting, deduping and throttling before chunking. gnomAD gained frequency lookup by variant id. ClinVar gained a throttle, MyGene gained chunking.

**Credits.** Advisors and funders are in `Authors@R`, both READMEs, the licence files and the docs home page. Posit Software, PBC is a copyright holder, and the three licence files say so.

**CRAN preparation.** biohttp is on CRAN now at 0.1.2, so `Remotes:` is gone and the pin is `biohttp (>= 0.1.2)`. Every network example moved from `\dontrun{}` to `\donttest{}`, 53 of them, because they can actually run. All 125 exported topics now cite the service behind them with a resolved DOI, and `Description` carries five anchor references in the form CRAN asks for. `cran-comments.md` holds the submission notes.

**CI runs everywhere now.** The workflows used to run only on a pull request into `main`, which is why PRs #15, #16 and #17 landed on `dev` with no checks at all. They now run on every pull request. `cran.yml` stays narrow on purpose: it makes 53 real requests to services we do not own.

## Is CRAN's biohttp new enough?

CRAN has 0.1.2, GitHub has 0.1.3 untagged. I checked rather than assumed:

- all 13 biohttp symbols this package calls are exported by 0.1.2
- `post_json_many()` in 0.1.2 already takes `throttle` and `max_tries`
- I installed the CRAN tarball into a separate library and ran the suite against it: 1099 passing, same as against 0.1.3

0.1.3 fixes `max_tries` doing nothing in the batched path. This package never passes it there, it only forwards `...`, so nothing here is affected.

## Checks

Locally, on the built `bioclients_0.1.1.tar.gz` with `R CMD check --as-cran`:

```
0 errors | 0 warnings | 3 notes
```

The notes are "New submission", plus missing pandoc and a `''NULL''` directory, both of which are my machine rather than the package. On CRAN this should be one note.

`checking examples with --run-donttest ... [107s] OK`, so all 53 live-service examples really ran. `checking tests ... [56s] OK`.

PR #13 was green on all 11 checks before merging into `dev`.

## Not in this PR

The tag and the release. Those come after this merges, so the tag points at what actually shipped.

title: chore: bring main back into dev
description:
`dev` never picked up PR #14, the Code of Conduct reporting contact, because that one merged straight into `main`.

Branch protection caught it. The release PR (#18) could not merge because `dev` was not up to date with `main`, and that rule was right to stop it: merging `dev` into `main` as it stood would have quietly reverted the reporting address and the confidentiality line.

This is the missing merge, nothing else. One file, three lines.

title: chore: prepare the package for CRAN submission
description:
Prepares bioclients for CRAN, and answers in advance the review comments that came back on biobouncer's first submission.

## Against the biobouncer feedback

| Comment | State here |
| --- | --- |
| Add references to the `Description` field | Applied. Nothing was cited before. |
| Never comment out code in examples | Already clean. The `\examples{}` block was extracted from all 126 `.Rd` files and every line matched; there were no commented lines. |
| Wrap `Suggests`-dependent examples in `requireNamespace()` | Already clean. Examples call only `biohttp` and `tibble`, both in `Imports`. |

The audit turned up one thing the reviewer did not raise for biobouncer but would raise here: all 53 network examples were in `\dontrun{}`. The CRAN Cookbook reserves that for examples that genuinely cannot run and puts data-downloading examples under `\donttest{}`. These are keyless public requests, so they are now `\donttest{}`.

That swap is safe for the reason the package exists. A client returns an envelope instead of raising, and biohttp's disk cache is off by default, so an example with no network prints `NULL` and writes nothing. Verified by running the examples behind an unroutable proxy: no error, no warning, all `NULL`, nothing written to the working directory.

## What changed

* **53 examples** move from `\dontrun{}` to `\donttest{}`.
* **All 125 exported topics gain a `References` section.** Each of the 29 service files carries one authored `@references` block on its primary client with the canonical publication, a DOI, and the service documentation URL; the rest of the file inherits it, so the citation is written once rather than copied 125 times. Every DOI was resolved through the CrossRef API and checked against the returned title, first author, year and pagination. Three of the initial candidates pointed at the wrong paper and were replaced: the ClinGen Allele Registry, VariantValidator, and MyVariant, which has no paper of its own and shares the Xin et al. web services paper with MyGene.
* **`Description` cites five anchors** in the requested `authors (year) <doi:...>` form: Ensembl, UniProt, gnomAD, Open Targets, AlphaFold DB. The other 24 stay on the help pages, which the closing sentence says.
* **Two service URLs corrected.** `https://gtexportal.org/` 301s, and `www.ensembl.org` geo-redirects to a mirror that was returning 504.
* **`pkg-r/cran-comments.md` added**, already covered by `.Rbuildignore`.
* **Version 0.1.1**, with `NEWS.md` and `CITATION.cff` moving alongside `DESCRIPTION`.

## Checks

`R CMD check --as-cran --run-donttest` on macOS 26.5.2, R 4.6.0: **0 errors, 1 warning, 1 note**. All 53 converted examples ran against the live services with no error and no warning.

* The warning is `Remotes:` and the unavailable `biohttp` dependency. See below.
* The note is `ensembl_gene_model` and `vep_variants` running over five seconds. Both are a single request to Ensembl and the elapsed time is entirely Ensembl's latency; CPU time is a rounding error. There is nothing left to make smaller, and `\donttest{}` is the wrapper CRAN prescribes for an example over five seconds.

Also clean: `devtools::test()` 893 passing, `lintr::lint_package()` no lints, `prek run --all-files` all hooks passing, tarball 211K.

## Not in this PR

`Remotes:` stays. `biohttp` is not on CRAN, and removing the line now would break dependency resolution on a clean runner for no gain. It comes out in a one-line commit at submission time, which cannot happen until biohttp is accepted first. `cran-comments.md` opens by saying so.

title: docs: add the Zenodo DOI and lift installation up the README
description:
Two commits.

## 1. The Zenodo DOI

The 0.1.0 release is archived. `CITATION.cff` gains both DOIs, and the README gains the badge and a citation section, so `citation("bioclients")` and GitHub's "Cite this repository" button both work.

**The badge uses the concept DOI (`…870`), not the version DOI (`…871`).** Zenodo's badge page hands you the version DOI by default, but that one pins 0.1.0 permanently, so the badge would still advertise 0.1.0 after 0.2.0 ships. The concept DOI always resolves to the newest release, which is what biohttp already does. Both are recorded, so pinning a version is still possible.

Also links the first mention of `biohttp` and `genescout`, both public. `variant-reviewer` is left unlinked because it is still private and the link would 404.

## 2. Installation moved up

It sat at **line 235 of 321**, so a reader who wanted to try the package had to scroll past the whole rationale first. Now at line 15, directly under the status block, followed by one worked call.

No table of contents, deliberately. GitHub already renders one from the headings and pkgdown builds its own sidebar, so a hand-written one duplicates both and goes stale.

The batch example further down was restating the envelope contract that now appears above it, so it is trimmed to input-order batching, which is its actual subject.

## Verification

- both DOIs return 200 through `doi.org`; `CITATION.cff` parses as valid CFF 1.2.0
- all three GitHub links resolve 200
- the promoted headline example re-run live: `ok`, 1 x 8, every column and value as printed
- `prek run --all-files`: passes
- `rcmdcheck` at CI settings: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes

title: feat: release 0.1.0
description:
Release gate for 0.1.0. Two commits: the version bump across the three files that declare one, and the merge.

`main` currently declares `0.0.0.9000`, so this is what makes the tree tagable. Once this merges, `main` is what `v0.1.0` points at.

## What changed

| File | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pkg-r/DESCRIPTION` | `0.0.0.9000` | `0.1.0` |
| `CITATION.cff` | `0.0.0.9000` | `0.1.0`, plus `date-released` |
| `pkg-r/NEWS.md` | development stub | first-release entry |

Both READMEs now install from r-universe in one call, and the GitHub route documents `subdir = "pkg-r"`, which was missing and fails silently when omitted.

## Verified before opening

- `rcmdcheck` at CI's exact settings: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes, banner reads `bioclients 0.1.0`
- `prek run --all-files`: passes
- no `0.0.0.9000` anywhere in the tree
- `CITATION.cff` parses as valid CFF 1.2.0

## After this merges

1. Tag `v0.1.0` on `main`
2. Create the GitHub Release, which is what Zenodo hooks
3. Add the concept and version DOIs to `CITATION.cff` and the DOI badge to both READMEs, matching what biohttp already carries

`Remotes:` stays until biohttp is somewhere CRAN can resolve.

title: feat: prepare the 0.1.0 release
description:
Three files declared a version and all three said `0.0.0.9000`, R's convention for an unreleased development tree. Tagging against that would mint a permanent DOI whose metadata disagreed with the package it points at.

| File | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pkg-r/DESCRIPTION` | `0.0.0.9000` | `0.1.0` |
| `CITATION.cff` | `0.0.0.9000` | `0.1.0`, plus `date-released` |
| `pkg-r/NEWS.md` | `# bioclients 0.0.0.9000` | `# bioclients 0.1.0` |

The NEWS heading is now a real first-release entry. The note explaining why the heading carried a version rather than the usual "(development version)" wording is gone, because at a real version there is nothing left to explain.

## Installation, which was the actual barrier

Both READMEs previously said bioclients was unpublished and installed from a local checkout. They now lead with r-universe, which resolves `biohttp` as a dependency, so it is one call:

```r
install.packages("bioclients", repos = "https://samuelbharti.r-universe.dev")
```

The GitHub route now documents `subdir = "pkg-r"`. That was missing, and an install that omits it fails without explaining why, since the package sits in a subdirectory rather than at the repository root.

The r-universe badge and install line will 404 until the `packages.json` sync lands. Expected, and self-correcting.

## Deliberately not in this PR

**No DOI badge and no `doi:` field.** Zenodo mints those from the GitHub Release, so they do not exist yet. biohttp carries both a concept DOI and a version DOI in `CITATION.cff`; bioclients gets the same in a follow-up once the numbers exist.

**`Remotes:` stays.** Correct for a GitHub and r-universe release, fatal for CRAN. It comes out when biohttp is somewhere CRAN can resolve.

## Verification

- `rcmdcheck` at CI's settings: **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes**, and the banner now reads `bioclients 0.1.0`
- `prek run --all-files`: passes
- `CITATION.cff` parses, `cff-version: 1.2.0`, matching the quoted date form biohttp already uses successfully with Zenodo
- no `0.0.0.9000` remains anywhere in the tree

title: feat: follow the biohttp release, confirm the port live, and publish the docs
description:
First release gate. Everything on `dev` since `main` was last updated, and the first CI run this repository has ever had.

## What is in it

**Unblocked the package.** biohttp shipped as 0.1.0, not 0.3.0, so the pin failed outright. Corrected, and `Remotes: samuelbharti/biohttp` added so a clean runner can resolve it. Verified by installing from GitHub with `GITHUB_PAT` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` both blanked, which proves the default CI token is enough and no secret is needed.

**Confirmed the port against live services.** Every parser was pinned by a stored response, but those responses were ported out of the apps rather than fetched. `test-live.R` calls all 29 services and asserts the five claims that had never been checked. Four held. The fifth did not: Monarch's two hosts serve all three routes with identical payloads, so they collapsed to one, and Monarch has one circuit breaker instead of two.

**Documentation.** The service table went from 8 rows to all 29. The roadmap, install section, dependency list and fixture provenance were all wrong and are now right. The package gained its own README, which is what puts the hex logo on the site. Three private sibling apps are no longer named.

**CI and the site.** Workflows narrowed to `pull_request: branches: [main]`, which is why this is the first run. pkgdown gained the deploy job, so merging this publishes the site.

## Verified locally before opening

Run at CI's exact settings rather than mine, which matters: `check-r-package@v2` does not pass `--as-cran` and defaults to `error-on: warning`.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `rcmdcheck`, `--no-manual`, no `--as-cran`, `error_on = "warning"` | 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes |
| `lintr::lint_package()` | 0 lints |
| `devtools::test()` | 893 passing, 1 skip, which is the live file |
| `prek run --all-files` | passes, including gitleaks |
| gitleaks over full history | 91 commits, no leaks |
| live run, `BIOCLIENTS_LIVE=true` | 90 passing, 2 failing, both Pharos |

Pharos was answering HTTP 502 from its own gateway. That is an outage, not a finding, and it does not affect this PR: the live file skips unless `BIOCLIENTS_LIVE` is set, and no workflow sets it.

## After merge

The push to `main` runs pkgdown and deploys to Pages, which is now enabled with GitHub Actions as the source. `Remotes:` has to come out before any CRAN submission.

title: fix: accumulate gnomAD populations without a superassignment
description:
`gnomad_parse_populations()` folded exome and genome counts together by having a nested function reach out with `<<-` and rewrite a list in its parent. The accumulator is now passed in and returned.

This is the one thing CI caught that a local run did not. lintr changed the default for `assignment_linter` to reject `<<-`; local lintr is 3.3.0.1, which still defaults to `operator = c("<-", "<<-")`, so `lint_package()` was answering a different question locally than on the runner.

Reproduced the runner's rule locally by passing `operator = "<-"` explicitly: **0 lints**. That also confirms `lint_package()` only covers `R/`, so the 51 `<<-` in the test request spies were never in scope.

- `devtools::test()`: 893 passing, 1 skip
- `rcmdcheck` at CI settings: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes

title: docs: refer to the unpublished sibling apps without naming them
description:
Three of the apps this package was ported from are not public: they were named 37 times across the README, CONTRIBUTING, and the call-site comments. That published the names and internal file layout of unreleased work, and left a public reader with references they cannot follow.

They are now referred to by the role they play. The provenance notes keep what makes them useful: that a behaviour was established somewhere real, and why the line sits where it does.

`genescout` and `variant-reviewer` stay named. Neither is staying private, and `genescout/R/tools/` is the reference layout this package follows.

Re-documenting also picked up two Rd files that had drifted: `bioclients-package.Rd` had never gained the logo figure or the documentation site URL from DESCRIPTION.

### Verification

- 0 references remain, checked for both the hyphenated and the spaced spellings
- offline suite: 893 passing, 1 skip (the live file)
- `prek run --all-files`: passes
- `rcmdcheck` at CI's exact settings (`--no-manual`, no `--as-cran`, `error_on = "warning"`): **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes**

title: test: confirm the ported behaviour against live services
description:
Closes roadmap phase 3.

Every parser here is pinned by a stored response, but those responses were ported out of the apps rather than fetched. A fixture cannot tell you a service changed its mind.

`pkg-r/tests/testthat/test-live.R` calls all 29 services once, then makes the specific assertions the five unchecked claims depend on. Gated on `BIOCLIENTS_LIVE`, `skip_on_cran()` and `skip_if_offline()`. No CI job sets the variable.

### What the run found

Four of the five held:

| Claim | Result |
| --- | --- |
| MyGene names the HGNC id `HGNC`, upper case | confirmed, `hgnc` absent entirely |
| Reactome answers 404 for a gene it maps with no pathways | confirmed via `ZNF876P` |
| PanelApp's index `search` does not filter | confirmed, searching Marfan returns the whole 434-panel index |
| Ensembl's VEP id route returns an array, not a record | confirmed, unnamed list of length 1 |
| Monarch needs two hosts | **refuted**, see below |

Monarch's two hosts serve all three routes with byte-identical payloads, same total and same ids in the same order. The comment on that client already said to collapse them once a live check confirmed it, so they are collapsed. One circuit breaker instead of two.

The run also turned up an undocumented trap: Ensembl takes `content-type` as a query parameter, not a header. Without it you get the HTML browser page with HTTP 200, so the call looks fine until the JSON parser reaches the first tag. Already handled in the client, now commented and pinned.

### Not confirmed

Pharos answered HTTP 502 from its own nginx gateway for the whole session, across roughly 20 requests over half an hour. That is an outage, not a finding about the port, and its check is left in place to say so next time.

### Verification

- live run: 90 passing, 2 failing, both Pharos
- offline suite: 893 passing, 1 skip, which is this file
- `prek run --all-files`: passes
- `rcmdcheck --as-cran`: 0 errors, 1 warning, 1 note, both unchanged and both known

title: fix: take the site colour from the logo
description:
The site kept the green it was given before the hex logo existed, so the navbar and link colour had nothing to do with the package's own mark.

Uses the logo's oxblood `#8a3a30` instead. The darker of the two warm tones rather than the amber, because this drives link text and the amber does not have the contrast for it on a light background. biohttp's site is set from its logo the same way.

Rebuilt and checked: `--bs-primary: #8A3A30`, link colour `#8A3A30` in the light theme and `#b98983` in the dark one, and no `#1a6b54` survives anywhere in the generated site.
